description: Establishes what the machine's defences were set to, and which of them had been moved off their stock default. Correlates the security posture set (Mark-of-the-Web handling, virtualisation-based security and Credential Guard, SMB signing and guest authentication) with the flat configuration set (fast startup, which decides whether a shutdown was a real one) and the Internet Explorer zone map, where a host promoted to Trusted Sites runs content every other zone would block. Answers the question the other wings assume: were the defences on at the time?
proves: A security control was moved off its default, changing what was possible on this machine
author: Crow-Eye Team

feathers.tier_name: Security setting against its stock default

semantic_rules.name: Security Control Off Its Default
semantic_rules.description: SecurityPosture stores every setting beside its stock default and records whether the two agree. 'changed' is that comparison, not a guess - so this rule fires on a value someone moved, and stays quiet on a machine where nothing was touched. The row's own meaning column says what the change permits.

semantic_rules.name: Mark-of-the-Web Suppressed
semantic_rules.description: SaveZoneInformation controls whether a downloaded file keeps the zone identifier that marks it as having come from the internet. Suppressed, files lose their origin and stop warning anyone - and the absence of a Mark-of-the-Web on a downloaded file stops being evidence that it was not downloaded. Read the row's assessment column: present-and-default is the normal state.

semantic_rules.name: LSASS Protection State
semantic_rules.description: Credential Guard decides whether LSASS ran protected, and therefore whether credential theft from memory was possible at all. This is context for a credential-access finding rather than a finding on its own: unset is the default on most consumer installs.

semantic_rules.name: Virtualisation-Based Security State
semantic_rules.description: Whether VBS was enabled. Recorded because it bounds what a kernel-level technique could have done, not because being off is itself suspicious - it is off on a great many ordinary machines.

semantic_rules.name: SMB Signing Not Required
semantic_rules.description: Without required SMB signing, traffic to this host can be relayed - which turns a captured authentication into access somewhere else. Pairs with any network logon evidence the lateral-movement wing found.

semantic_rules.name: Insecure Guest Logons Allowed
semantic_rules.description: Insecure guest authentication permits unauthenticated SMB access to a share, so a connection can leave no account behind to attribute it to.

semantic_rules.name: Host Promoted To Trusted Sites
semantic_rules.description: Zone 2 is Trusted Sites, where content runs that every other zone blocks. A host placed here is a deliberate act - the interesting row is one nobody in the organisation recognises.

semantic_rules.name: Host Placed In Restricted Sites
semantic_rules.description: Zone 4 is Restricted Sites. Recorded for completeness: it is the opposite of a weakening and is usually policy, but it is part of the same picture of how the zone map was arranged.

semantic_rules.name: Fast Startup Masks A Shutdown
semantic_rules.description: With fast startup on, a shutdown hibernates the kernel session instead, so ShimCache is never flushed and an empty ShimCache proves nothing. The same fact the anti-forensics wing records, kept here because it belongs to the posture picture too.

semantic_rules.name: Event Log Channel Disabled
semantic_rules.description: A disabled channel explains a silence. Several ship disabled by default - TaskScheduler/Operational and DNS-Client/Operational among them - so judge against that list before calling it tampering.
